claims.claimText: An acceleration transducer configured to detect a force acting in a rectangular coordinate system with three axes disposed orthogonally with respect to each other, and including a transverse axis, a longitudinal axis and a vertical axis, the acceleration transducer comprising: a main body defined by a first tangential side face, a second tangential side face, a third tangential side face, a fourth tangential side face, a first normal side face and a second normal side face, wherein each of the tangential side faces is disposed tangentially with respect to the vertical axis, and wherein each of the normal side faces is disposed normally with respect to the vertical axis; a first piezoelectric electric element defined in part by a first end face and a second end face disposed spaced apart from the first end face and parallel to the first end face, wherein the first end face lies in a first plane that is defined by the vertical axis and the longitudinal axis, wherein the second end face lies in a second plane that is defined by the vertical axis and the longitudinal axis and spaced apart along the transverse axis from the first plane, wherein the first piezoelectric element is secured to the first tangential side face of the main body and configured to generate piezoelectric charges on the first and second end faces under the action of a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; a first seismic mass secured to the first piezoelectric electric element in a manner to receive a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis and proportional to an acceleration acting on the main body and to exert a shear force proportional to the acceleration along the longitudinal axis onto the first piezoelectric element, which is configured to generate piezoelectric interference charges on the first and second end faces under the action of a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; a first electrically conductive end face coating on the first end face of the first piezoelectric element, a second electrically conductive end face coating on the second end face of the first piezoelectric element, wherein each of the first and second electrically conductive end face coatings is configured to receive piezoelectric charges generated for the shear force acting along the longitudinal axis, wherein each of the first and second electrically conductive end face coatings is configured to receive interference piezoelectric charges generated for the shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; wherein the first piezoelectric element is further defined by a first lateral surface, a second lateral surface, a third lateral surface, and a fourth lateral surface, wherein each of the lateral surfaces lies in a plane that is disposed parallel to the vertical axis; wherein the first seismic mass is attached to the first piezoelectric element in a manner exerting upon acceleration a normal force proportional to the acceleration and acting along the longitudinal axis onto the first piezoelectric element, which is configured to generate piezoelectric interference charges on the lateral faces of the first piezoelectric element under the action of the normal force acting along the longitudinal axis; and a first electrically conductive lateral coating configured to receive piezoelectric interference charges generated for the normal force along the longitudinal axis, wherein the first electrically conductive lateral coating covers a first area of the first lateral surface of the first piezoelectric element.

An acceleration transducer as in claim 1, further comprising: a second piezoelectric electric element defined in part by a first end face and a second end face disposed spaced apart from the first end face and parallel to the first end face, wherein the first end face lies in a first plane that is defined by the transverse axis and the vertical axis, wherein the second end face lies in a second plane that is defined by the transverse axis and the vertical axis, wherein the longitudinal axis is disposed in a direction that is normal to the first plane and the second plane, wherein the second piezoelectric element is secured to the second tangential side face of the main body and configured to generate piezoelectric charges on the first and second end faces under the action of a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; a second seismic mass secured to the second piezoelectric electric element in a manner to receive a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis and proportional to an acceleration acting on the main body and to exert upon the acceleration a shear force proportional to the acceleration along the longitudinal axis onto the second piezoelectric element, which is configured to generate piezoelectric interference charges on the first and second end faces under the action of a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; a first electrically conductive end face coating on the first end face of the second piezoelectric element, a second electrically conductive end face coating on the second end face of the second piezoelectric element, wherein each of the first and second electrically conductive end face coatings is configured to receive piezoelectric charges generated for the shear force acting along the longitudinal axis, wherein each of the first and second electrically conductive end face coatings is configured to receive interference piezoelectric charges generated for the shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; wherein the second piezoelectric element is further defined by a first lateral surface, a second lateral surface, a third lateral surface, and a fourth lateral surface, wherein each of the lateral surfaces lies in a plane that is disposed parallel to the vertical axis; wherein the second seismic mass is attached to the second piezoelectric element in a manner exerting upon acceleration a normal force proportional to the acceleration and acting along the longitudinal axis onto the second piezoelectric element, which is configured to generate piezoelectric interference charges on the lateral faces of the second piezoelectric element under the action of the normal force acting along the longitudinal axis; and a first electrically conductive lateral coating configured to receive piezoelectric interference charges generated for the normal force along the longitudinal axis, wherein the first electrically conductive lateral coating covers a first area of the first lateral surface of the second piezoelectric element.

An acceleration transducer as in claim 2, further comprising: a third piezoelectric electric element defined in part by a first end face and a second end face disposed spaced apart from the first end face and parallel to the first end face, wherein the first end face lies in a first plane that is defined by the vertical axis and the longitudinal axis, wherein the second end face lies in a second plane that is defined by the vertical axis and the longitudinal axis, wherein the transverse axis is disposed in a direction that is normal to the first plane and the second plane, wherein the third piezoelectric element is secured to the third tangential side face of the main body and configured to generate piezoelectric charges on the first and second end faces under the action of a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; a third seismic mass secured to the third piezoelectric electric element in a manner to receive a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis and proportional to an acceleration acting on the main body and to exert a shear force proportional to the acceleration along the longitudinal axis onto the third piezoelectric element, which is configured to generate piezoelectric interference charges on the first and second end faces under the action of a shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; a first electrically conductive end face coating on the first end face of the third piezoelectric element, a second electrically conductive end face coating on the second end face of the third piezoelectric element, wherein each of the first and second electrically conductive end face coatings is configured to receive piezoelectric charges generated for the shear force acting along the longitudinal axis, wherein each of the first and second electrically conductive end face coatings is configured to receive interference piezoelectric charges generated for the shear force acting along the longitudinal axis; wherein the third piezoelectric element is further defined by a first lateral surface, a second lateral surface, a third lateral surface, and a fourth lateral surface, wherein each of the lateral surfaces lies in a plane that is disposed parallel to the vertical axis; wherein the third seismic mass is attached to the third piezoelectric element in a manner exerting upon acceleration a normal force proportional to the acceleration and acting along the longitudinal axis onto the third piezoelectric element, which is configured to generate piezoelectric interference charges on the lateral faces of the third piezoelectric element under the action of the normal force acting along the longitudinal axis; and a first electrically conductive lateral coating configured to receive piezoelectric interference charges generated for the normal force along the longitudinal axis, wherein the first electrically conductive lateral coating covers a first area of the first lateral surface of the third piezoelectric element.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 1, wherein the first piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for the shear force exerted along a principal tangential axis by the first seismic mass, which principal tangential axis is disposed within the rectangular coordinate system; wherein the first piezoelectric element has a low sensitivity for the shear force exerted by the first seismic mass along a secondary tangential axis, which lies along a direction that is normal to the principal tangential axis; and wherein the first piezoelectric element has a low sensitivity for a normal force exerted along a normal axis by the first seismic mass, wherein the normal axis lies along a direction that is normal to each of the principal tangential axis and the secondary tangential axis.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 1, wherein the first piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the principal tangential axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a normal force along the transverse axis being the normal axis; or wherein the first piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the normal axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a shear force along the transverse axis being the principal tangential axis; or wherein the first piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the principal tangential axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a normal force along the transverse axis being the normal axis.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 1, wherein the first piezoelectric element is configured with a high sensitivity for a shear force along a principal tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a shear force along a secondary tangential axis or a normal axis; and wherein the first piezoelectric element is configured so that a high sensitivity for a shear force generates at least by a factor of 5 times more piezoelectric charges per unit force than a low sensitivity for a shear force.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 1, wherein the first electrically conductive end face coating and the first electrically conductive lateral surface coating form a first continuous electrically conductive coating; and wherein the piezoelectric interference charges picked off for the shear force along the secondary tangential axis have a polarity opposite to that of the piezoelectric interference charges picked off for the normal force along the normal axis.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 7, wherein a size of the first electrically conductive lateral surface coating of the first piezoelectric element is configured in such a way that the first continuous electrically conductive coating picks off essentially the same number of piezoelectric interference charges for the shear force acting along the secondary tangential axis and for the normal force acting along the normal axis.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 7, wherein the first lateral face includes a first portion that is disposed normal to the tangential axis of the first piezoelectric element; wherein the first lateral surface includes a first further electrically conductive lateral surface coating; wherein a ratio of a size of the first electrically conductive lateral surface coating and a size of the first further electrically conductive lateral surface coating is configured in such a way that the continuous electrically conductive coating picks off essentially the same number of piezoelectric interference charges for the shear force acting along the secondary tangential axis and for the normal force acting along the normal axis.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 9, further comprising a first piezoelectric element conductor and a second piezoelectric element conductor; wherein the first electrically conductive lateral surface coating is materially bonded to the first piezoelectric element conductor; wherein the further first further electrically conductive lateral surface coating is materially bonded to the second piezoelectric element conductor; wherein the first piezoelectric element conductor is configured to transmit piezoelectric charges as a plurality of first acceleration signals from the first continuous electrically conductive coating; and wherein the second piezoelectric element conductor is configured to transmit piezoelectric charges as a plurality of second acceleration signals from the second continuous electrically conductive coating.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 10, wherein the first electrically conductive end face coating is material bonded to the first end face and configured to seal microscopic pores in the first end face; wherein the first electrically conductive lateral surface coating is material bonded to the first lateral surface and configured to seal microscopic pores in the first lateral surface; and wherein that as a result of the sealing of the microscopic pores eliminates the need to the mechanically pre-load the first piezoelectric element.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 1, wherein each of the first end face and second end faces is disposed in a manner opposite to the normal axis of the first piezoelectric element; wherein the first lateral surface is disposed normal to the secondary tangential axis of the first piezoelectric element; wherein the first lateral surface includes a first further electrically conductive lateral surface coating; wherein the first electrically conductive end face coating and the first electrically conductive lateral surface coating form a first continuous electrically conductive coating; and wherein the second electrically conductive end face coating and the first further electrically conductive lateral surface coating form a second continuous electrically conductive coating.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 2, wherein the second piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the principal tangential axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a normal force along the transverse axis being the normal axis; or wherein the second piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the normal axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a shear force along the transverse axis being the principal tangential axis; or wherein the second piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the principal tangential axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a normal force along the transverse axis being the normal axis.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 3, wherein the third piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the principal tangential axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a normal force along the transverse axis being the normal axis; or wherein the third piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the normal axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a shear force along the transverse axis being the principal tangential axis; or wherein the third piezoelectric element has a high sensitivity for a shear force along the vertical axis being the principal tangential axis, a low sensitivity for a shear force along the longitudinal axis being the secondary tangential axis and a low sensitivity for a normal force along the transverse axis being the normal axis.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 12, wherein the second and third lateral surfaces is disposed normal to the principal tangential axis of the first piezoelectric element; wherein the second lateral surface includes a second electrically conductive lateral surface coating; wherein the third lateral surface includes a third electrically conductive lateral surface coating; and wherein the second and third electrically conductive lateral surface coatings are part of the first continuous electrically conductive coating or part of the second continuous electrically conductive coating.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 15, wherein the fourth lateral surface is disposed normal to the secondary tangential axis of the first piezoelectric element and includes a fourth electrically conductive lateral surface coating; and wherein the second and fourth electrically conductive lateral surface coatings are part of the first continuous electrically conductive coating or part of the second continuous electrically conductive coating.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 12, wherein the second and third lateral surfaces is disposed normal to the principal tangential axis of the first piezoelectric element; wherein the second lateral surface includes a second electrically conductive lateral surface coating; wherein the third lateral surface includes a third electrically conductive lateral surface coating; and wherein the third electrically conductive lateral surface coating is part of the first continuous electrically conductive coating and the second electrically conductive lateral surface coating is part of the second continuous electrically conductive coating.

The acceleration transducer according to claim 17, wherein the fourth lateral surface of the first piezoelectric element is disposed normal to the secondary tangential axis of the first piezoelectric element; wherein the fourth lateral surface includes a fourth electrically conductive lateral surface coating; wherein the third electrically conductive lateral surface coating is part of the first continuous electrically conductive coating, and wherein the fourth electrically conductive lateral surface coating is part of the second continuous electrically conductive coating.
